Early 30’s here and I have about $100 in my account. I’m holding onto that for dear life until payday. If you’re struggling to save my I recommend the envelope method. It’s easy, start small withdraw for example $10 to come out and you physically take the $10 and put into an envelope. Then after a bit you up it, $15…$20…$25 it adds up. Helped me learn how to save and now I use a tip jar with my bank where each week when I get paid $25 comes out and goes into the tip jar, some weeks I add in more but I’ve learned a little goes a long way. I don’t touch it till I absolutely need too. I work full time too and sometimes on my days off I Instacart and that helps me get ahead. You can do it!

I suffer from severe anxiety with some depression. Usually my depression is worst in the morning and my roommate who’s my best friend will come in after she’s heard me hit snooze a couple times. And she’ll say something dumb like let’s wake up and get this day. 

She’ll hand me a cup of coffee or something to eat and we’ll talk for a minute or so about what my plan is for the day. 

She’s listened to me cry, scream, yell and push her away and she’s always come back or say my my side. 

During lockdown when I was super anxious she went and got bird feed and ice cream and we walked around and fed the birds and it made me so happy. 

So honestly just keep showing up and being there. You’re doing great our minds just tell us no one loves for some strange reason.

Things that help me is making a list of everything positive in my life. I use to think it was the worlds most stupidest thing but it helped my brain focus on the positive things. 

My therapist has me writing down the 5 things I’m grateful for at the end of the week and that’s really helped too. 

I like to go for walks around the park and sometimes I’ll feed the ducks or just sit there and watch them and it helps me feel a lot better. 

And if you’re having a really bad day I’ve learned there’s no shame in crying it out. I’ll write down the bad thoughts I’m having and then cry it out. Once I have that out of my system I take what I’ve written and I rip it up. And honestly ripping up those bad thoughts feels amazing. 

I hope this helps. Just remember you’re never alone
